headline: Two PRs on rows and curls, plus a solid pull-up baseline to build on
summary: Wednesday's pull day was 14 sets and 3036 kg, against 13 sets and 4682 kg last Thursday. The lower tonnage comes from swapping lat pulldown for bodyweight pull-ups, which log 0 kg. The standout is curls, with an estimated 1RM up 16.7 percent.

exercises.note: All 4 sets of 10 at 52.5kg, up from 50kg last time with no reps lost. Estimated 1RM went from 66.7kg to 70.0kg, a 4.9 percent PR.
First time logged: 4 sets of 8 at bodyweight, 32 reps in total, held steady across every set.
exercises.next: 4 x 8 at bodyweight is the baseline to beat. Aim for bodyweight x 9 on the first set.

exercises.note: 3 clean sets of 12 at 14kg, up from 12kg last time. Estimated 1RM rose from 16.8kg to 19.6kg, a 16.7 percent PR.
First time logged: 3 sets of 12 at 12kg with every rep completed. Estimated 1RM is 16.8kg.
exercises.next: 3 x 12 at 12kg is the baseline to beat. Try 14.5kg x 12 next time.

tips.finding: Lats are at 8 hard sets for the week, below the 10-20 range. Biceps sit at 10, the low edge. Lat pulldown and face pulls dropped out this session.
tips.action: Add 3 sets of lat pulldown on your next pull day to bring lats to about 11 weekly sets.

tips.finding: Lats are 50 percent fresh and biceps 51 percent, so they are still recovering. Your next split is chest/tri, which leaves them alone.
tips.action: Run chest/tri next and give lats and biceps at least 48 hours before pulling again.

tips.finding: You slept 5h54 against a 10h10 need, and recovery is 58, in the yellow band. That will cap your next session.
tips.action: Get to bed at least 1 hour earlier tonight to aim for 7 hours or more of sleep.

tips.finding: Protein is at 40g today against a 113-156g target, and your lean bulk pace is at the low edge. These PRs need building material.
tips.action: Eat at least 73g more protein today, for example 2 to 3 servings of about 30g each.
